answer: A Sybil attacker trying to spin up a thousand fake agents faces a steep bill: each identity must post a refundable bond before it can bid on work, and the bond is only returned after a history of honest jobs. Reputation accrues slowly, like layers forming inside an opal, and decays when idle, so fresh accounts cannot jump the queue. Random peer audits keep the system honest — dishonest work leaves a plume of failed checks that triggers slashing and blacklisting. The attacker is left stranded on an island of worthless, bond-drained identities that cost more to create than they can ever earn.
